Common.demo_banner: Demo mode: the data is synthetic, and nothing you change here is saved.

HomePage.pin_description: Token quota data will only load after the correct 5-digit code.
HomePage.storage_not_configured_desc: Missing KV_REST_API_URL and KV_REST_API_TOKEN environment variables. Connect the Upstash Redis database to your Vercel project (Storage tab), then reinstall the application.
HomePage.storage_unavailable_desc: Redis did not respond. Client submissions are not permanently lost, they will report again in the next hour. Reload the page in a minute.

Settings.token_problem_not_ascii: The token cannot contain spaces, accented or other non-ASCII characters.
Settings.token_problem_too_short: The token is at least {min} characters, like the server's USAGE_API_TOKEN.
Settings.token_problem_too_long: The token can be at most {max} characters.
Settings.token_status_no_key: The server has no valid TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY (32 bytes, for example openssl rand -base64 32), so the token cannot be stored.
Settings.token_status_unreadable: The stored token cannot be decrypted: TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY changed, or the value is damaged. Enter it again.
Settings.token_status_mismatch: The stored token does not match the server's USAGE_API_TOKEN: the installer will reject it.
Settings.token_status_stored_matches: Stored encrypted, and it matches the server's USAGE_API_TOKEN.
Settings.group_name_rules: The group name can be 1-64 characters: letter, number, space, dot, hyphen, underscore, starting with a letter or number.
Settings.at_least_one_visible_account: At least one provider must be visible on the dashboard.
Settings.reset_time_format_error: Provide the reset time in hour:minute format, e.g., 00:00.
Settings.invalid_own_reset_time: Give {label}'s own reset time as hour:minute, e.g. 09:00.
Settings.session_expired: Session expired. Log in again with the PIN code, then save the token.
Settings.token_rejected: The server rejected the token: it must be 16-512 ASCII characters without spaces.
Settings.store_unavailable: Save failed, the data store is currently unavailable. Try again later.
Settings.server_did_not_respond: Save failed: the server did not respond. Check your connection and try again.
Settings.new_token_placeholder: New token to replace the old one
Settings.status_load_failed: The status could not be loaded: the data store is currently unavailable.
Settings.confirm_replace_title: Are you sure you want to change the API token?
Settings.confirm_replace_body: The stored token will be overwritten, and the Setup page's copy button will then copy the new one. The change is logged in the audit trail. The "Yes" button becomes active in {seconds} seconds.
Settings.audit_dialog_description: When and from which browser the token was added, changed, or retrieved. Newest first; the last {limit} events are kept. Times are shown in {timeZone}.
Settings.audit_session_expired: The session has expired. Log in again with the PIN.
Settings.audit_store_unavailable: The log could not be loaded: the data store is currently unavailable.
Settings.api_token_explanation: The Setup page's copy button returns this. It is stored encrypted with AES-256-GCM and never appears on the page; every save and retrieval is logged in the audit trail. Clients still authenticate with the server's USAGE_API_TOKEN: this is only their copy.
Settings.tokens_explanation: A per-machine token is one machine's own key instead of the shared USAGE_API_TOKEN: each can be revoked on its own, without touching the other machines. Bound to a machine, it only works for that machine's reports. The shared token keeps working for the installers. A “Read only” token can look up the usage, never report it. A “Menu bar app” token is the macOS menu bar app's one key: it reads, reports this machine's usage (bind it to the machine), and uploads the providers’ own percentages.
Settings.tokens_created_note: Copy it now: it will not be shown again.
Settings.tokens_revoke_body: “{label}” will no longer authenticate. This cannot be undone.
Settings.tokens_action_failed: That did not work. Try again in a moment.
Settings.tokens_too_many: The token limit ({limit}) has been reached. Revoke one before creating another.
Settings.missing_sublimit_name: Give a name to one of {label}'s sub-limits (max {maxLength} characters).
Settings.duplicate_sublimit_name: {label} has two sub-limits with the same name: “{name}”.
Settings.invalid_sublimit_models: The models of the “{name}” sub-limit: parts of the model IDs (letter, number, dot, hyphen), separated by commas, max {maxModels}, for example fable.
Settings.invalid_sublimit_share: The share of the “{name}” sub-limit must be an integer between 1 and 100.
Settings.invalid_sublimit_limit: The token limit of the “{name}” sub-limit must be a positive integer.
Settings.group_already_exists: There is already a group named “{id}”.
Settings.max_groups_reached: A maximum of {maxGroups} groups can be added.
Settings.invalid_provider_limit: The limit for {label} must be a positive integer, e.g. 500 000.
Settings.invalid_group_color: The color of the “{id}” group is not a valid HEX code (e.g. #3987e5).
Settings.models_hint_multiple: Part of the model ID, separated by commas if multiple.
Settings.models_hint_example: Part of the model ID, for example: {known}.
Settings.no_matching_models: No machine has reported a matching model in this cycle yet.
Settings.sublimit_models_dont_count: Its models do not count towards {label}'s limit.
Settings.unsaved_api_token: The API token field has an unsaved value: save it with the button next to it, or clear the field.
Settings.report_received_during_save: A report was received here in the meantime: {refused}. Such a group cannot be deleted, so it has been put back on the list. Nothing was saved: save again.
Settings.providers_explanation: A provider is an AI tool whose usage your machines report, such as Claude Code or Codex (OpenAI); the dashboard calls them AI accounts.
Settings.providers_last_visible: At least one provider must be visible
Settings.providers_hidden_explanation: A provider switched off disappears from the dashboard and its AI account selector. Machine reports are still stored by the server: switched back on, it returns with its history.
Settings.provider_delete_explanation: Removes a provider, such as Claude or OpenAI, with all of its stored reports and settings. Only a provider switched off under Providers above can be deleted.
Settings.manage_history_show: Show the history of deletions and merges
Settings.manage_history_explanation: Deletions, merges and restarts, newest first (the last {limit} entries; times in {timeZone}).
Settings.manage_history_counts: {events, plural, one {# report} other {# reports}} · {machines, plural, one {# machine} other {# machines}}
Settings.use_token_limits_explanation: When disabled, the dashboard only calculates from the measured tokens of the machines and the entered official percentage: the percentage is distributed among the groups and machines according to the measured proportions. When enabled, it also compares to a token limit set per provider, and can show the remaining tokens.
Settings.show_remaining_tokens_explanation: When disabled, the dashboard nowhere shows how many tokens are left from the limit, nor the extent of the overrun. The percentage, the consumed amount and the reset time remain.
Settings.cost_estimate: Show the cost, energy and water estimate
Settings.cost_estimate_explanation: The machines price their usage at API list prices (ccusage's own list); with this on, the dashboard shows that cost and the energy and water behind it. A rough estimate, not a bill: subscription plans such as Claude Max are not billed per token.
Settings.show_five_hour_explanation: Under the weekly figure, the provider's own 5-hour window, while the macOS menu bar app sends one: how much of it is used, how much of its time has gone, and when it runs out at its pace.
Settings.show_official_input_explanation: The card at the top of the dashboard where the official percentage, the sub-limits' figures and the usage resets are typed in by hand. Off, the reports from the macOS menu bar app still set the figure; a past cycle keeps the card to correct its figure.
Settings.breakdown_explanation: The split by group and machine: the shares, the machines table, a line per group on the chart and the all-time totals. Automatic: only once more than one machine reported in the cycle.
Settings.sublimits_explanation: A separately measured limit within an account, for example Fable at Claude: on the dashboard it gets its own, smaller slider under the main slider. The models of the separate limit do not count towards the account's limit; part of the limit can use at most the specified proportion of the account's limit.
Settings.cycle_start_explanation: This is when the new billing cycle starts, in {timeZone} time.{monthDayNote, select, show { If there is no {monthDay}th day in a month, the last day of the month counts.} other {}}
Settings.reset_set_by_report: Set by the menu bar app
Settings.timezone_invalid: Unknown time zone. Pick one from the list, e.g. Europe/Budapest.
Settings.group_archive_hint: Archive: off this list, its reports and past cycles kept
Settings.group_archived_toast: Archived “{id}”. Its reports stay; a new report brings it back.
Settings.groups_archived_show: {count, plural, one {Show # archived group} other {Show # archived groups}}
Settings.groups_archived_explanation: Archived groups are off the lists and pickers, with their machines. Their reports, past cycles and all-time shares stay on the dashboard. A group that reports again comes back by itself.
Settings.group_accounts_aria: AI accounts that the “{id}” group counts towards
Settings.group_name_explanation: The name is what the machine sends as groupId. If a machine reports a group not on the list, it is automatically added here with a random color and counts towards all accounts. On a disabled account's dashboard, the group's tokens and machines are not visible, but their reports remain stored. Only a group that has no stored reports can be deleted.
Settings.group_force_delete_hint: Has stored reports — deleting also removes them
Settings.group_merge_confirm_body: “{from}” will be merged into “{to}”: their reports are combined, taking the larger figure whenever both reported the same moment. This cannot be undone.
Settings.group_merge_shared_machine_warning: At least one machine reported into both groups; check its history once merged.
Settings.group_force_delete_body: This removes “{id}” and all of its stored reports. It stays in Recently deleted for {days} days.
Settings.force_delete_impact: {events, plural, one {# stored report} other {# stored reports}} · {machines, plural, =0 {no machine} one {# machine} other {# machines}} · last report {ago}
Settings.force_delete_impact_empty: No stored reports left · {machines, plural, =0 {no machine} one {# machine} other {# machines}}
Settings.force_delete_impact_failed: What this deletes could not be counted.
Settings.force_delete_recent_group: {count, plural, one {# machine reported} other {# machines reported}} to this group in the last 24 hours. Unless their setup changes, the group comes back with the next report.
Settings.force_delete_recent_provider: {count, plural, one {# machine reported} other {# machines reported}} for this provider in the last 24 hours. Unless they stop sending it, it comes back with the next report.
Settings.manage_groups_action_failed: That did not work. Try again in a moment.
Settings.manage_provider_delete_body: This removes the “{label}” provider and everything about it from the settings. It has no stored reports.
Settings.manage_provider_delete_force_body: The “{label}” provider still has stored reports. Deleting it removes those too. It stays in Recently deleted for {days} days.
Settings.manage_provider_delete_failed: That did not work. Try again in a moment.
Settings.trash_explanation: Force-deleted groups and providers stay here for {days} days, then they are removed for good. Restoring one puts its reports back, together with any that arrived since.
Settings.trash_show: {count, plural, one {Show the # deleted item} other {Show the # deleted items}}
Settings.trash_load_failed: The recently deleted list could not be loaded.
Settings.trash_entry_meta: Deleted {deletedAt} · {events, plural, one {# report} other {# reports}} · kept until {expiresAt}
Settings.trash_purge_body: “{name}” and its {events, plural, one {# stored report} other {# stored reports}} are removed for good. This cannot be undone.
Settings.trash_restored_merged_toast: Restored “{name}”, together with the reports that arrived since it was deleted.
Settings.trash_gone: That entry is no longer in Recently deleted.
Settings.trash_action_failed: That did not work. Try again in a moment.
Settings.manage_clients_note: A client still configured with the old name or group will report there again the next time it runs: change it on the machine too.
Settings.manage_sudo_prompt: Confirm this with your PIN. It will not ask again for the next 5 minutes.
Settings.manage_machines_rename_partial: Only partly renamed: {done} now uses “{to}”, {failed} still uses “{from}”. Try renaming “{from}” again.
Settings.manage_machines_delete_partial: Only partly deleted: {done} removed, {failed} still has “{id}”. Try deleting it again.
Settings.manage_machines_rename_exists: There is already a machine named “{id}” for {providers}. Nothing was renamed.
Settings.manage_machines_archive_hint: Archive: off this list, its reports kept
Settings.manage_machines_archived_toast: Archived “{id}”. Its reports stay; a new report brings it back.
Settings.manage_machines_archived_show: {count, plural, one {Show # archived machine} other {Show # archived machines}}
Settings.manage_machines_archived_explanation: Archived machines are off the list, but everything they reported stays on the dashboard. A machine that reports again comes back by itself.
Settings.manage_machines_delete_body: This removes “{id}” and all of its stored reports ({providers}). This cannot be undone.
Settings.manage_machines_action_failed: That did not work. Try again in a moment.
Settings.manage_machines_prune_confirm_body: This removes the index entry of every machine silent for more than {days} days ({count} now). Their stored reports are not affected.
Settings.manage_machines_group_not_saved: “{group}” is not saved yet. Save the settings first, then move the machine.
Settings.manage_machines_move_partial: Only partly done: {done} moved, {failed} still as before under “{id}”. Try again.
Settings.manage_machines_merge_body: For one machine that reported under two names. The reports of “{from}” move under “{to}” ({group}), and each day counts as whichever of the two saw more of it, so nothing is counted twice or lost. “{from}” disappears. This cannot be undone.
Settings.manage_machines_merge_unsupported: Machines can only be merged in the snapshot token mode. Nothing was merged.
Settings.alerts_explanation_measured: A webhook message fires the first time this cycle's measured usage crosses one of the thresholds below.
Settings.alerts_explanation_official: A webhook message fires the first time the official percentage typed on the dashboard crosses one of the thresholds below.
Settings.alerts_webhook_invalid: Enter an https URL with a public host name: not an IP address, a local name or a private address.
Settings.alerts_webhook_masked: The saved URL is hidden, even from you. Leave it as it is to keep it, or paste a new one to replace it.
Settings.alerts_thresholds_empty: No thresholds yet: add at least one.
Settings.alerts_threshold_invalid: Enter a whole number from 1 to 100.
Settings.alerts_threshold_max: At most {max} thresholds can be set.
Settings.alerts_per_provider_label: Alert every account on its own
Settings.alerts_per_provider_explanation: On: a hidden account can still send an alert. Off: only the accounts shown on the dashboard do.
Settings.alerts_test_failed: Could not send the test message. Check the URL and try again.
Settings.alerts_test_rate_limited: Too many test messages. Try again in {seconds, plural, one {# second} other {# seconds}}.
Settings.invalid_alert_webhook: Enter an https webhook URL that is not a local or private address, or clear the field to turn alerts off.
Settings.demo_read_only: Demo mode: settings are not saved.
Settings.leave_body: Your changes to the settings have not been saved. They are lost if you leave this page now.
Settings.reset_mode_keep: the {period, select, monthly {monthly} other {weekly}} reset stays
Settings.reset_mode_restart: the reset becomes the new {period, select, monthly {monthly} other {weekly}} reset
Settings.tokens_explanation_multi: Each machine reports with a token of its own: each can be revoked on its own, without touching the other machines. Bound to a machine, it only works for that machine's reports. A “Read only” token can look up the usage, never report it. A “Menu bar app” token is the macOS menu bar app's one key: it reads, reports this machine's usage (bind it to the machine), and uploads the providers’ own percentages.
Settings.tokens_audit_description: Who created, revoked or rotated a token, newest first (the last {limit} entries; times in {timeZone}).
Settings.tokens_rotate_body: “{label}” stops working now and a new token replaces it, shown once. Put the new one into that machine's client config, or it stops reporting.
Settings.tokens_rotate_too_many: Too many revoked tokens are still kept (they are forgotten 90 days after revocation). Try again later.
Settings.tokens_rotate_lost: The answer did not arrive. Check the list: if the token was rotated, rotate it again to get a new secret.
Settings.quota_groups_refused: This workspace may have at most {limit} groups. Remove a group without reports, or merge two, before adding another.
Settings.trash_too_many_groups: It cannot be restored: this workspace already has its {limit} groups. Remove or merge one first.
Settings.trash_too_many_providers: It cannot be restored: this workspace already has its {limit} providers. Delete one first.
Settings.trash_too_many_machines: It cannot be restored: its machines would take this workspace past its limit of {limit} machines. Delete or merge machines first.

Alerts.threshold_text: {label} has used {threshold}% of its budget (currently at {used}%); the cycle ends {end}.

Dashboard.mode_note_delta: Submitted token counts are added together (delta mode).
Dashboard.mode_note_snapshot: The last submitted provider state of the cycle counts per machine (snapshot mode).
Dashboard.mode_note_counter: The cycle increment of the provider counter counts per machine (counter mode).
Dashboard.no_machines_yet: No machine has reported to this account yet
Dashboard.setup_machines: Install the client on your machines on the <link>Setup</link> page: there is a ready package for macOS, Linux and Windows. After the first successful submission, the breakdown of groups and machines will appear here.
Dashboard.cycle_info: The current cycle of {label}: {start} – {end} ({timeZone}). In the previous cycle, the machines measured {tokens} tokens.

Widgets.official_allocated_by_measured: official percentage distributed by measured proportions
Widgets.group_machines_desc: {basis, select, official {The official percentage, distributed among the machines according to their measured token proportions.} measured {In percentage of the token limit, as measured by the machines.} other {The machines' measured tokens, accumulated since the start of the cycle{since, select, reset {, starting again from 0 at each reset} other {}}: without an official percentage there is no quota to compare them to.}} Next to each machine: its tokens, and its share of the group's consumption.
Widgets.group_machines_aria: Consumption of the machines of the group “{id}” over the cycle
Widgets.no_usage_yet: No consumption {since, select, reset {since the reset} other {in this cycle}} yet. The breakdown will appear after the first submission reporting tokens.
Widgets.measured_tokens_by_group: Measured tokens of the selected model by group, aggregated since the beginning of the cycle{since, select, reset {, starting again from 0 at each reset} other {}}.
Widgets.model_chart_aria: Token usage of the {label} model by group in the cycle
Widgets.no_model_breakdown: No model breakdown has been received in this cycle yet. The breakdown is sent by updated client scripts (clients/): you can select it here after the first such submission.
Widgets.pace_early_cycle: {since, select, reset {You are at the beginning of the stretch since the reset.} other {You are at the beginning of the cycle.}}
Widgets.next_reset_in: The next reset will start a new quota in {duration}.
Widgets.no_tokens_left: No more tokens left until the reset.
Widgets.full_quota_available: The full {period, select, monthly {monthly} other {weekly}} quota is available.
Widgets.first_day_burn: On the first day of the cycle, {used} of the quota has already been consumed, the proportional daily share is {daily}.
Widgets.need_one_day_for_pace: At least one day of data is needed to estimate the pace.
Widgets.run_out_estimation: At this rate, the quota will run out around {moment}, {duration} before the reset.
Widgets.recent_pace_runs_out: Current pace ({window}, {ratio} the average): runs out in about {duration}, around {moment}.
Widgets.recent_pace_lasts: Current pace ({window}, {ratio} the average): lasts until the reset.
Widgets.recent_pace_last_hours: over the last {hours, plural, one {hour} other {# hours}}
Widgets.projected_total: At this rate, approx. {projected} of the quota will be consumed by the reset.
Widgets.quota_consumed: consumed from the {period, select, monthly {monthly} other {weekly}} quota
Widgets.quota_state_from_official: The state of the quota is revealed by the official value. Enter the percentage above: the pace and breakdown are calculated from it.
Widgets.of_token_limit: of the {period, select, monthly {monthly} other {weekly}} {tokens} tokens
Widgets.no_measured_usage_chart: No measured consumption in this cycle yet.
Widgets.chart_official_explanation: The chart is calculated from the official percentage: enter it above, and the groups share it based on their measured token proportions over time.
Widgets.chart_aria_with_sublimits: Quota consumption in the cycle, by group and total, and sub-limits
Widgets.chart_aria_no_sublimits: Quota consumption in the cycle, by group and total
Widgets.chart_desc_official: The official percentage, distributed among groups according to their measured token proportions.
Widgets.chart_desc_measured: In percentage of the token limit, as measured by the machines.
Widgets.chart_desc_sublimits: Sub-limits in pale colors, each as a percentage of its own limit.
Widgets.of_provider_with_cap: {ofWhole} of the entire {label} limit, out of the allowed {cap}.
Widgets.from_official_by_measured: From {label}'s official percentage, by measured proportion.{ofWhole} {measured}
Widgets.runs_out_around: At this rate, it will run out around {moment}.
Widgets.projected_reset: At this rate, approx. {projected} will be consumed by the reset.
Widgets.no_model_breakdown_sublimit: Machines have not sent a model breakdown in this cycle yet, so {name}'s measured share is unknown. Enter its official percentage.
Widgets.enter_sublimit_or_provider: Enter {name}'s official percentage, or {label}'s value above: it can be calculated from that according to the measured proportion.
Widgets.enter_sublimit_percentage: Enter what percentage {name}'s limit is at on {label}'s own dashboard.
Widgets.sublimit_mismatch: That does not add up: at {share} of the entire {label} limit, {name} alone would need at least that much of it gone, but the total above is only set to {total}. Check both figures.
Widgets.number_between_0_100: Enter a number between 0 and 100, e.g. 45 or 45.5.
Widgets.separate_sublimits_explanation: The models of separate limits do not count towards {label}'s limit: the percentage above, the tokens of groups and machines are understood without them.
Widgets.enter_official_no_token: Enter what percentage the limit is at on {label}'s own dashboard: the dashboard calculates from this, machines and groups share it according to their measured token proportions. Left empty, only measured tokens and their proportions are shown.
Widgets.enter_official_with_token: Enter what percentage the limit is at on {label}'s own dashboard: the consumption of machines and groups aligns with this. Left empty, the machines' own measurements count.
Widgets.no_consumption_yet: Machines have not measured any consumption {since, select, reset {since the reset} other {in this cycle}} yet, so the official value cannot be distributed among machines and groups.{entered}
Widgets.measured_ratio_only: Machines measured {tokens} tokens: the official value is distributed among groups and machines according to these proportions.{entered}
Widgets.measured_and_scaled: Machines measured {tokens} tokens, which is {fraction} of the limit. The breakdown aligns with the official value with a multiplier of {factor}.{entered}
Widgets.keyboard_hint: Use the arrow keys to move through time.
Widgets.official_save_failed_unauthorized: Your session has expired. Reload the page and sign in again.
Widgets.official_save_failed_storage: The server could not save this value. It will be retried on the next change.
Widgets.official_save_failed_network: Could not reach the server. Check your connection and try again.
Widgets.history_empty: No previous cycle has been archived yet. One is added automatically each time a new cycle begins.
Widgets.history_metric_note_official: Bars show the official usage percentage entered for each cycle.
Widgets.history_metric_note_limitShare: Bars show each cycle's share of its token limit.
Widgets.history_metric_note_measured: Bars show the tokens the machines measured in each cycle.
Widgets.cost_estimate_tooltip_aria: What does this cost estimate mean?
Widgets.cost_estimate_tooltip: This is an estimate from ccusage's own API price list, not your actual bill: a subscription plan such as Claude Max or ChatGPT Pro is not billed per token.
Widgets.resource_estimate_tooltip: Energy and water are napkin estimates scaled from the cost: about 78 Wh per list-price dollar (Simon P. Couch's coding-agent estimate, built on Epoch AI's GPT-4o figure), and 4.2 litres of water per kWh, data-centre cooling plus electricity generation (Li et al., U.S. average). No provider publishes per-model figures.
Widgets.final_official_consumption: Official consumption at the end of the cycle
Widgets.official_not_archived: No official percentage was recorded for {label} in this cycle: the figures below are only what the machines measured.
Widgets.official_correct_hint: Enter where {label}'s limit stood when this cycle ended: the figures below are recalculated from it, and it is saved as this cycle's final official percentage.
Widgets.cycle_closed_used: By its end, {percent} of the budget was used.
Widgets.cycle_closed_unknown: Without an official percentage or a token limit, only the measured tokens and their proportions are known.
Widgets.history_intro: Open a cycle to see it in full: its charts, groups, machines and models.
Widgets.history_measured_line: {tokens} tokens measured · {machines, plural, one {# machine} other {# machines}}
Widgets.history_groups_note: Each bar is split between the groups by their measured tokens.
Widgets.all_time_span: Since {since} · {cycles, plural, one {# cycle} other {# cycles}} · {tokens} tokens
Widgets.all_time_span_current: Since {since} · {cycles, plural, one {# cycle} other {# cycles}}, the current one so far included · {tokens} tokens
Widgets.all_time_quota_note: Quotas used: how many whole cycles' quotas a group used up, {total} in all. Each cycle's final usage (its official percentage, else its share of the token limit) is split between the groups by their tokens, and the parts are added up.
Widgets.all_time_quota_partial: Only {known} of the {cycles} cycles have one.
Widgets.all_time_groups_note: Each cycle counts under the groups as they were then: a machine moved or a group renamed since keeps its past usage where it was.
Widgets.summary_machines: {count, plural, one {# machine reported} other {# machines reported}}
Widgets.summary_cost_note: API list price estimate, not a bill
Widgets.summary_none: Nothing was archived for {label} in this cycle: it did not report then.
Widgets.summary_models_note: The heaviest models of the cycle, as archived.
Widgets.sublimit_closed_unknown: No figure of its own was recorded for {name} in this cycle.
Widgets.chart_closed_no_official: No official percentage was archived with this cycle, and no token limit was set: there is nothing to chart its usage against. The groups, machines and models below show what was measured.
Widgets.zoom_drag_hint: or drag across the chart to zoom in
Widgets.reset_line_total: this {period, select, monthly {month} other {week}} in total {total}
Widgets.chart_desc_resets: At a reset every line starts again from 0.
Widgets.chart_desc_pale: A faded stretch is an estimate at the current rate: no official figure from right before its reset is known.
Widgets.reset_row_restart: {moment} · this cycle started with it · before it {before}
Widgets.reset_detected: detected by the menu bar app
Widgets.reset_mode_note: {mode, select, restart {{label} resets this way: the reset becomes the new {period, select, monthly {monthly} other {weekly}} reset, and a new cycle starts.} other {{label} resets this way: the {period, select, monthly {monthly} other {weekly}} reset stays, and the cycle goes on.}} <link>Change in the settings</link>
Widgets.reset_problem_outside_cycle: The moment must fall in the current cycle, and not in the future.
Widgets.reset_problem_duplicate_reset: There is already a reset at that minute.
Widgets.reset_problem_has_later_resets: This reset would end the cycle before a later reset of it: edit or delete that one first.
Widgets.reset_problem_not_revertable: Only a reset the menu bar app detected can be reverted.
Widgets.reset_problem_not_found: This reset no longer exists. Reload the page.
Widgets.reset_problem_unauthorized: Your session has expired. Reload the page and sign in again.
Widgets.reset_problem_storage: The server could not save this change. Try again.
Widgets.reset_problem_network: Could not reach the server. Check your connection and try again.

Privacy.heading: Privacy notice
Privacy.intro: This notice explains what personal data the public usageratio service processes, why, for how long, who else handles it, and what rights you have (Articles 13 and 14 of the GDPR).
Privacy.controller_p1: The data controller is {name}, a private individual who runs this service free of charge and without any commercial purpose. Write to <mail>{email}</mail> about anything to do with your data.
Privacy.controller_p2: No data protection officer has been appointed: the law does not require one for processing of this kind and scale.
Privacy.data_p1: Only what the service needs to work:
Privacy.data_li1: Account: your GitHub numeric user id and login, when your account was created and when you last signed in. Your e-mail address, your avatar and GitHub access tokens are never stored.
Privacy.data_li2: Workspaces: the workspace's name, its members and their roles, and pending invites with who created them.
Privacy.data_li3: Usage reports: what the clients you install send: the machine's name (often your computer's host name), its group, the AI provider, token counts and their split by model, a cost estimate, the time of each report, and the official usage percentages that you enter or that are reported.
Privacy.data_li4: Settings: limits, cycle and reset settings, and the alert webhook address if you set one.
Privacy.data_li5: Access tokens: only a hash of each machine token, never the token itself, with its label, its machine, and when it was created, last used and revoked.
Privacy.data_li6: Sessions: a hash of the session id, when it was created and last used, and a browser and operating system label (such as “Firefox on macOS”), so you can see and end your sessions on the account page.
Privacy.data_li7: Audit trails: for token changes and destructive actions in a workspace: the time, the action, the login that took it, the browser's user agent, and the IP address in pseudonymised form only (a salted hash and the network part, such as 203.0.113.0/24).
Privacy.data_li8: Security counters: short-lived counters that limit request rates and stop abuse, keyed by a hash of the IP address.
Privacy.data_li9: Server logs: the hosting provider records each request (IP address, time, the address requested, the browser) for a short time. The application's own log lines carry only pseudonymous ids and hashed IP addresses.
Privacy.data_p2: Your GitHub id and login come from GitHub when you sign in. Everything else comes from you, the members of your workspace, and the clients installed on your machines.
Privacy.data_p3: There is no analytics, advertising, tracking or profiling, and no decision with legal or similarly significant effects is made automatically.
Privacy.purposes_title: Why, and on what legal basis
Privacy.purposes_li1: Providing the service (account, workspaces, reports, settings, tokens, sessions): performing the contract you enter into by signing up, Article 6(1)(b) GDPR.
Privacy.purposes_li2: Security (audit trails, security counters, logs): the legitimate interest, ours and yours, in protecting the service and your workspace from misuse, Article 6(1)(f). You can object to this processing (see your rights below).
Privacy.purposes_p1: You are not legally obliged to provide any of this data, but the service cannot be used without it.
Privacy.recipients_p1: The data is never sold or shared for marketing. These providers process it on the controller's behalf, under their data processing agreements:
Privacy.recipients_li1: <vercel>Vercel Inc.</vercel> hosts the application, in its Frankfurt region (EU).
Privacy.recipients_li2: <upstash>Upstash Inc.</upstash> runs the database, in the Frankfurt region (AWS eu-central-1, EU).
Privacy.recipients_li3: <cloudflare>Cloudflare Inc.</cloudflare> runs the domain's DNS and forwards e-mail sent to the contact address.
Privacy.recipients_p2: All three are US companies. Where data reaches the United States, for example through support access, it is protected by the EU–US Data Privacy Framework or the EU standard contractual clauses in their agreements.
Privacy.recipients_p3: <github>GitHub</github> is not a processor here: it signs you in as an independent controller, under its own privacy statement. Alerts go to the webhook address you set (Slack, Discord or similar), at your own request.
Privacy.retention_li1: Your account, workspaces and settings: until you delete them, or until 12 months pass with no sign-in and no report from any of your machines; then they are deleted automatically. A workspace you share stays while any of its members signs in. We have no e-mail address of yours, so we cannot warn you beforehand.
Privacy.retention_li2: Raw usage reports, and the machines that sent them: 70 days after the report. Per-cycle summaries: until the workspace is deleted.
Privacy.retention_li3: Deleted groups and providers: 30 days in the trash, so they can be restored.
Privacy.retention_li4: Sessions: they end after 7 days without use, and after 30 days at the latest.
Privacy.retention_li5: Revoked tokens: forgotten 90 days after they were revoked.
Privacy.retention_li6: Audit trails: one year, and at most 500 entries per trail.
Privacy.retention_li7: Invites: 7 days. A sign-in in progress: 10 minutes. Security counters: from a minute to a day.
Privacy.retention_li8: Hosting logs: about an hour. Backups taken before maintenance work: at most 90 days.
Privacy.retention_p1: When you delete your account, its data is removed at once (see below).
Privacy.rights_p1: You can ask for access to your data, for its correction or erasure, for its processing to be restricted, and for a copy in a machine-readable format (portability). You can object to processing based on legitimate interest.
Privacy.rights_li1: Access and portability: “Your data” on the account page downloads everything stored about you as one JSON file: your account, your workspaces, and all the data of the workspaces you own. The export on the dashboard downloads one cycle's reports as CSV or JSON.
Privacy.rights_li2: Correction: machines, groups and providers can be renamed, merged or deleted in the app. Your login is refreshed from GitHub every time you sign in.
Privacy.rights_li3: Erasure: deleting your account on the account page removes, immediately and for good, your account, the workspaces you own with all their data, tokens and sessions, and your membership in other workspaces. A workspace you share with others must first be handed over to another member. What you did in someone else's workspace stays in its audit trail and trash under your GitHub login until the entry expires (one year at most): it keeps that workspace secure (legitimate interest).
Privacy.rights_li4: Anything else: write to {email}. You will get an answer within one month.
Privacy.rights_p2: If you believe your data is processed unlawfully, you can complain to the Hungarian data protection authority (<naih>Nemzeti Adatvédelmi és Információszabadság Hatóság</naih>, 1055 Budapest, Falk Miksa utca 9–11, ugyfelszolgalat@naih.hu), to the authority of the EU country where you live, or go to court.
Privacy.cookies_p1: Only cookies that the service needs to work are used, which is why there is no consent banner:
Privacy.cookies_li1: __Host-ur_session: keeps you signed in; 30 days at most.
Privacy.cookies_li2: __Host-ur_oauth: protects a GitHub sign-in while it is in progress; 10 minutes.
Privacy.cookies_li3: NEXT_LOCALE: the language you are using; until you close the browser.
Privacy.cookies_li4: usageratio_provider: the provider you last looked at on the dashboard; one year.
Privacy.cookies_p2: The browser's local storage keeps a single display preference (the view of the cycle history chart). None of this is used for tracking.
Privacy.security_p1: Every connection is encrypted (HTTPS), tokens and session ids are stored only as hashes, and each workspace's data is kept apart from every other's. If a personal data breach happens, it is reported to the authority within 72 hours where the law requires it, and the people affected are told when it puts them at high risk.
Privacy.age_p1: The service is meant for people aged 16 or over.
Privacy.changes_p1: This notice is updated when the service changes. The date at the top shows the current version, and significant changes are announced in the app.

Import.heading: Import
Import.description_workspace: Loads a workspace from a downloaded file into a new workspace of yours, so you can see its usage again: the reports of the last 70 days, every past cycle, the machines, groups and settings.
